text.p: Following are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At the board's meeting last Saturday the Democratic Party Saimnieks decided to stay in cabinet despite the departure of leader Ziedonis Chevers.
- The Ministry of Economy has prepared several plans to encourage Latvians to use their privatisation vouchers.
- Talks on the delimitation of the border between Russia and Latvia will continue in Riga on October 31 and November 1.
- The heads of the state-owned TV channels of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia met last Friday in Riga to discuss the problems of public television in the Baltics.

- Last week the Latvian Board of Harbours considered amendments to the Law On Harbours which would introduce tax privileges for companies working in the territory of small ports. The board also considered restoring the port of Ainazi on the border with Estonia.
- The Latvian Gas company is building a modern gas-metre station on the border with Estonia.
- Latvia could become a full-fledged member of the World Trade Organisation in 1997.
